pull_request.title: feat(nexus-agent): the Nexus Agent tool, released beside the app from its mirror
pull_request.body:
Stage F of issue #3130, Tasks 2, 3 and 4 (plan: PR #3190), pull request B: the Nexus Agent feature as a protocol 2 tool. Nothing of the Vitruvian app changes here (that is PR C). Needs SDK 1.1.0 for the kit's waker, which is released.

## What this does

- **The tool lives in the standalone app's package**, `apps/desktop/nexus-agent/macos`, as new targets on the shared engine (`NexusAgentCore`): SwiftPM resolves only a repository root, and the shared libraries sit there. MIT, with the feature's texts carried out as the shared library was (63 keys, fifteen languages).
- **Core:** the tool's settings as a `NexusAgentHost` (eight preferences, what is handed taken once), its pages (an island page that is the way to the window plus a glance, a Settings panel), four commands (Quick Prompt, new chat, start and stop the bot).
- **Program:** AppKit on the main thread beside the kit's thread, joined by the kit's waker so the main thread never waits on the kit; the Quick Prompt window; the Telegram bot adopted by PID file so it keeps running across the hand-off.
- **Release:** the mirror's `release.yml` zips the tool's folder beside the app's assets, named by the tool's version, with its size and checksum in the notes; the rehearsal workflow follows, held in step by `nexus_agent_release_rehearsal_test`.

## Checked on the final tree, after merging main

`NexusAgentToolTests` (20), the standalone's `NexusAgentTests` (263, unchanged), `tool_conformance_test` (the built tool validates; a panel of 5 blocks, and a new page after a tap), `tool_version_test`, the rehearsal drift test, the pin tests, `upstream_test`; conformance check 430 ok, 0 fail; presubmit generator `--check`; licence verify; `//:tidy`. SwiftPM on a scratch copy built and ran both test bundles. Planted regressions each failed their test and were reversed (settings taken twice; a panel registered under the wrong id; a rehearsal step renamed). No test reaches this Mac's Nexus Agent settings or bot.

## Not proven here

Nothing was seen on screen. The mirror's build, zip and folder-check steps first run on the mirror at the next Nexus Agent release.

feat(vitruvian-sdk): a tool can hand work to its thread from another

The kit gains ToolWaker: tool.waker.later takes work from any thread,
a window's or a child process's, and runs it on the kit's thread as soon
as it is between messages, after the hello, never while a handler runs or
waits for the app. The wire polls a wake pipe beside standard input; an
error the handed work throws goes to the tool's log. The guide says so
and the site's copy is synced. Stage F, Task 1 of issue #3130.

fix(nexus-agent): the tool's tests set up on the main actor, for the CI Mac's Swift

The two test classes are held to the main actor, and their plain setUp()
and tearDown() touch the classes' own properties. Swift 6.4 lets that by;
Swift 6.1.2, the CI Mac's (Xcode 16.4), refuses it in Swift 6 mode, which
is how SwiftPM builds this target: 28 errors, all in those four methods,
on this pull request's first run. They are async now, so the overrides
run on the actor. Bazel builds the same files in Swift 5 mode and never
saw it.

SwiftPM writes Package.resolved now that the package has a dependency; no
package here commits one, so it is ignored.

fix(vitruvian-sdk): what comes while handed work waits is answered when it is done

What failed: the Nexus Agent tool's conformance test on the CI Mac, at
"unknown: no answer within 2 seconds", right after the Quick Prompt
command ran. It passed on a developer's Mac.

Why: the Swift kit lost track of a message. Showing the Quick Prompt
hands the kit a badge to set, which is a request to the app. While the
kit waited for the badge's answer, the app's next command arrived and was
kept for later, as it should be. But after handed work the loop went
straight back to waiting for a new message and did not look at what it
had kept. The command sat there until the next message or timer, here up
to five seconds, and a goodbye would have dropped it unanswered. It is a
race: it only shows when the command arrives before the badge's answer,
which the slower CI Mac does and a fast Mac does not. Putting a logging
relay between the conformance script and the tool reproduces it here
every time, and a sample of the stuck tool shows its thread in
Tool.serve, waiting in poll, with the command never handled.

The fix: after handed work, the loop handles what was kept before it
waits again. A kit test hands work that calls the app, sends a command
before the answer, and expects the command answered with nothing more
sent; it failed before the change. Only the Swift kit hands work across
threads, so the other kits have no such path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(nexus-agent): the tool wakes the kit after each piece of handed work

What failed: built by SwiftPM, as the public mirror builds it, the tool
still left a command unanswered for up to five seconds after the Quick
Prompt was shown. SwiftPM takes the kit from the published SDK, 1.1.0,
which goes back to waiting after handed work without looking at what the
app sent while that work waited for an answer. The kit is fixed in this
repository, but the mirror cannot have that fix until the SDK is
released, and the rehearsal's check of the tool's folder runs against
the published kit.

The fix: every piece of work the tool hands to the kit's thread ends by
waking the kit, which makes it look at what it kept. With a kit that
looks by itself this does nothing more than one empty turn of its loop.
It can go once Package.swift asks for the fixed kit.

How it was checked: the tool built with `swift build` against SDK 1.1.0,
with the SDK's conformance script run through a relay that slows the
link a little. Before: "unknown: no answer within 2 seconds", every
time. After: all six checks pass, three runs of three.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ci): the rehearsal fetches the kit before it checks the tool's folder

What failed: the rehearsal's "Check the tool's folder" step, in the job
that packages the apps, with "find: apps/desktop/nexus-agent/macos/
.build/checkouts: No such file or directory".

Why: the step builds `vitruvian-tool` and takes the conformance script
from SwiftPM's checkout of the SDK. That checkout exists only where
SwiftPM has run. The package job starts from a fresh copy of the
repository and downloads what the build job built; the artifacts do not
carry what SwiftPM fetched to build it.

The fix: the step runs `swift package resolve` first, which fetches the
kit by the same rule in Package.swift the build job followed. It is one
line, in the one step that needs it. Passing the kit through an artifact
would change the upload both workflows share for a check only the
rehearsal makes, and the Homebrew formula has no bottle, so it would
build the same command from source at a version the tap chose, not the
one the package asks for.

release.yml is unchanged: the step is the rehearsal's alone, since a
release attaches the zip and judges nothing. The drift test now also
fails when a job of either workflow reads .build/checkouts without
having run a SwiftPM command first; it failed on the old step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
